description: A geometry library for engineering drawings and models, in two dimensions and in three. Points, vectors, lines, polylines, polygons, faces with holes, circles and oriented rectangles in the plane; points, planes, triangles, polygons, faces, solids, boxes, coordinate systems and transformations in space. Over both: distance, projection, containment, intersection, collision, parallelism, parametrization, merging, splitting, extending and trimming, offsetting, and boolean operations. It also carries the label placement algorithms that arrange drawing labels clear of each other and of blocked regions, and packs boxes such as drawing views onto sheets of paper. Every comparison is tolerance-aware, because coordinates that come out of a BIM model are never exact.
releaseNotes:
NEW IN 11.2.0

      NEW, a net body with its open cuts closed
      - TrySubtractAll takes SolidClosingOptions as well, and then closes a cut it would skip: the cut worked out within
        the tolerance is closed by GeoSolid3.TryClose, and where that does not close, the cut within the fallback. A
        body closed is taken only where it is valid within the booleans' tolerance too and holds what a cut can leave,
        no more than the body before the cut and no less than that less the whole tool. Every cut taken without closing
        is taken as before, bit for bit, and the overload without closing is unchanged.
      - No cut is closed where the body before it or the tool carries openings: such a cut is skipped as without
        closing.
      - SubtractReport says which cuts were closed (Closed, counted in Taken), how (Closings), and which closed but were
        refused for their volume (RefusedByVolume, still in Skipped).

      Of the 79 864 parts of a Tekla model cut within a thousandth with a contact and a fallback of a hundredth, 17 have
      a cut skipped, 35 of their 314 cuts; closing within a gap of 0.005 takes 9 of them and leaves 10, none refused for
      its volume, and the parts whose bodies cut within a hundredth are valid come out within 0.12 % of those, where
      skipping left them up to 10 % off.

      Details in CHANGELOG.md.

      Earlier releases: https://github.com/nguyenthanguth/GeometryHelper/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
